## d5869f5c395e

**Finding: reproduced canonical-coverage shortcut.** A plausible rival follows the legend mapping but draws a span only when the selected same-color pair shares a row or column. Ordinary generator draws choose legends only from `[5, 6, 4]` and construct horizontal/vertical pairs, so the rival matches the generated curriculum while avoiding the diagonal operation. A 2,000-draw deterministic probe found 2,000 axis-aligned selected pairs, 0 diagonal selected pairs, and 0 other legends (`checks/audit/sample-probes.json`).

The exact disagreement is the canonical test grid in `checks/audit/d5869f5c395e/input.json`. Its legend value `7` selects the two color-4 cells at `(5,1)` and `(8,4)` (zero-based), which are diagonal. The rival returns an all-zero output (`checks/audit/d5869f5c395e/rival.json`); the selected Racket authority paints the diagonal cells `(5,1),(6,2),(7,3),(8,4)` cyan, recorded in `checks/audit/d5869f5c395e/racket.json` (rule hash `c33c9bf33cd3`, generator SHA-256 `d9499af21b32464c6138c68b096742673de544ca8bb41b5eda896f2e1995b2a1`).

This target has no `self_check`, so validator acceptance is unavailable. The input is the exact canonical test input and unquestionably belongs to the task domain. The current proposed generator does not emit this legend-7 diagonal case. No source was changed because this was an audit-only target.

## d5869f5c395e

**Classification: reproduced summary and distribution divergence.** The current
summary says legends are in `{4,5,6}`, selected pairs are axis-aligned, the
selected span is painted in place, and the legend plus other pairs remain.
Canonical authority behavior includes a legend-7 branch selecting color 4,
accepts diagonal endpoints, and returns a fresh blank grid containing only the
cyan segment.

The retained canonical 10×11 input has legend 7 and diagonal color-4 endpoints
at `(5,1)` and `(8,4)`. Racket returns four diagonal color-8 cells and zeros
everything else. The summary-derived rival preserves the legend/distractors and
paints the line in place, leaving nine nonzero cells. Exact grids and source
binding are in `checks/audit/d5869f5c395e/counterexample.json`; the authority
receipt is `checks/audit/d5869f5c395e/racket.json`.

This input is canonical authority data but lies outside the generator's declared
and default domain; there is no callable `self_check` to expose that mismatch.
The generator therefore cannot reproduce a canonical branch and its natural
language contract predicts the wrong output even on a canonical example. Repair
should first align summary/output semantics, then add legend 7 and diagonal
examples plus a validator that accepts all canonical inputs.

Reproduction from `packet_root`:

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply d5869f5c395e \
  --input ../checks/audit/d5869f5c395e/input.json \
  --out ../checks/audit/d5869f5c395e/racket.json
```

Generator SHA-256: `d9499af21b32464c6138c68b096742673de544ca8bb41b5eda896f2e1995b2a1`.
Executed rule hash: `c33c9bf33cd3`.
